html:
A strong earthquake that struck Constantinople and the region around it early in 447. It brought down 57 towers and long stretches of the new Theodosian Walls, finished only about three decades before.

It came at a terrible moment. Attila and the Huns were raiding the Balkans and could march on the capital. The praetorian prefect Constantine put the circus factions of the Hippodrome, the Blues and the Greens, to work, some 16,000 people in all. They rebuilt the walls in about two months and added an outer wall and a moat. An inscription on one gate boasts of the speed.

Attila did not try to take the city. He ravaged the Balkans as far south as Thermopylae, and Theodosius II bought peace with a large payment of gold.
